newsitem.title: GREECE: Probe ordered into Greek ship rescue attempts.
newsitem.headline: Probe ordered into Greek ship rescue attempts.

text.p: A Greek court on Monday ordered an investigation into allegations that rescue teams delayed reaching a ship which capsized in the Aegean Sea, leaving nine people dead and 11 missing.
"The naval court chief prosecutor has ordered me to carry out an investigation into possible liability of the coastguard and the navy in alleged delays," deputy prosecutor Nikos Makris told Reuters.
The Greek cargo ship Distos capsized on Saturday in bad weather off the port of Kimi on the island of Evia.
The vessel had a crew of 18. The wife and 10-year-old daughter of one crew member and the wife of another were also on board.
Only one person was rescued -- 18-year-old nautical college student Christos Anagnostou.
"Unfortunately there is slim hope that the missing are still alive. We believe they were trapped inside the ship and drowned," a merchant marine ministry official said.
Court officials allged that rescue crews reached the Distos only after a 10-hour delay.
Five coastguard officers were suspended on Monday after being accused of delaying telling senior merchant marine ministry officials of the accident.
"There were certainly delays and nobody has yet given me an explanation why," Merchant Marine Minister Stavros Soumakis said.
Anagnostou told the coastguard two big waves engulfed the ship, which was carrying cement.
He jumped into the sea after the Distos started listing and shot flares into the air, helping the coastguard to spot the capsized vessel.
The ship, owned by the Heracles cement company, was carrying 5,300 tonnes of cement from the central port town of Volos to Piraeus, near Athens.
Many passenger vessels were advised to cancel voyages on Saturday because of storms in the Aegean.
